key_insight: Coarse-mesh graph neural networks predict sparse flow observables without reconstructing the full flow field, matching or outperforming finer-mesh surrogates at lower training cost.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports efficient prediction, system identification, and state estimation when engineers need only selected probes or integrated flow quantities.
method: Train graph neural networks directly on coarse meshes to predict sparse observables.
Select training parameters adaptively using variations in flow frequency spectra.
Use noise-augmented multi-step unrolling to improve long-horizon autoregressive predictions.
evidence_signal: Tests on parameterized 2D/3D confined cylinder flows and an unevenly heated cavity showed generalization to unseen conditions; adaptive sampling reduced maximum errors by an order of magnitude versus uniform sampling.
watch_item: Generalization beyond the tested geometries and Reynolds/Rayleigh-number ranges remains unestablished.
paper_title: Predicting Sparse Observables in Parameterized Unsteady Flows Using Coarse-Mesh Graph Neural Networks
